question: radial running clearance of the bayonet collar in the radome socket band across the capsule envelope, per manufacturing route, and the board ceiling it leaves (00_07 HW.33 / HW.9)

routes: coarse: IT8 collar · IT12 moulded band
inputs.routes_are: ours — the bracket axis until the vendors answer

routes.route: coarse: IT8 collar · IT12 moulded band

controls.closing_sign: zero at T_ref, opening at the hot edge

verdict: The cold edge closes the collar's running clearance by 30 µm radially at the capsule requirement −40 °C (both parts at it), 37 µm if the Ti stays at 20 °C — that is the physics floor. The design clearance the drawing must specify is the floor plus the tolerance of the route: 0.082–0.088 mm with both surfaces machined, up to 0.212–0.218 mm for a coarse moulding — every row stays below the 0.3 mm that 52 puts there for want of a number; at the print-floor wall 0.2 mm the board ceiling becomes 19.53–19.81 mm instead of 19.37 (design_to 20.37). The row is the drawing's fit, and the route that pins it is the vendors'.
ceilings: the routes' grades and roundness are ours until the vendors answer (DMLS / CNC / moulding letters, paused)
the radome PEEK grade is open — the CTE sensitivity row stands for it
capillary water in a narrow gap and its ice are not modelled — the drainage requirement governs them
friction, wear and creep of the turning fit are not modelled
